heroHeadline: Helion Valued at $15.5B After $465M Series G; CFS ARC Physics Validated by 58 Scientists; SPARC ~75% Complete
heroSubtitle: A watershed week for commercial fusion energy: Helion Energy closed a $465 million Series G round at a $15.5 billion valuation on June 4 — nearly 3× its January 2025 valuation — led by Thrive Capital with participation from Alta Park Capital, Lux Capital, Peak XV, and Bill Ford, bringing total capital to $1.5B and funding construction of the Orion power plant in Malaga, Washington (targeting 50 MW delivery to Microsoft by 2028). The same day, Commonwealth Fusion Systems published five peer-reviewed papers in the Journal of Plasma Physics co-authored by 58 scientists from MIT, Columbia, UC San Diego, KTH, Chalmers, and Max Planck, confirming ARC will produce 1.1 GW fusion power and 400 MW net electricity to the grid in the early 2030s. On June 2, Pacific Fusion's subscale pulser prototype delivered 440 GW in 80 nanoseconds, unlocking the next tranche of its $1B+ Series A, with demo facility construction starting this summer. ITER's Magnet Cold Test Facility completed the first 4 Kelvin cooldown of toroidal field coil TF07 on June 1, reducing integration risk. On June 7, Scientific American and Hackaday featured CFS's April 28 PJM Interconnection application as a historic infrastructure milestone — fusion energy has moved from laboratory to grid queue. Global private fusion investment now exceeds $10.6 billion.
footerNote: Data sourced from DOE/LLNL/NNSA, ITER Organization, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Helion Energy, Pacific Fusion, ARPA-E, UK Government, Fusion for Energy, ANS Nuclear Newswire, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Physical Review Letters, Journal of Plasma Physics, Fusion Science and Technology), and the Fusion Industry Association. All milestones independently verified.
